---
title: When AI builds itself
author: Anthropic
date: 2026-09-18
---

For most of AI's history, humans drove every step in its development cycle.
But at Anthropic, we are delegating a growing share of AI development to AI
systems themselves, which is speeding up our work.

Taken far enough, and given enough compute, that trend points to an AI
system capable of fully autonomously designing and developing its own
successor. This is called recursive self-improvement.

## Evidence from the outside world

The rate at which AI models improve is accelerating. The length of tasks
that they can reliably complete on their own has been doubling roughly
every four months.

The same pattern appears on coding and research benchmarks. SWE-bench is a
standard test of real-world software engineering.

## Evidence from within Anthropic

Building a frontier model takes two broad categories of work: engineering
and research.

Claude writes a significant proportion of Anthropic's code. As of May 2026,
more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic's codebase was authored by
Claude.

## What might the future of work at Anthropic look like

The evidence suggests that the human role is narrowing at each step in the
AI development process.

## What if we're wrong

A natural objection to the evidence presented above is that none of this
proves recursive self-improvement is close.

## Possible futures

What happens next depends on two things: whether these trends continue, and
how institutions respond.

## What should we do

If it were possible to effectively slow the development of these systems,
we believe that would be worth considering.
